title: Visual Disabilities & How People See (or Don’t) 👁️
description: Blindness, low vision, colour blindness – and how users navigate the web.

slides.title: The Visual Spectrum 🌈
slides.content:
Visual disabilities aren't just total blindness. They include:

* **Blindness** – no useful vision, rely on screen readers & braille.
* **Low Vision** – can see but need magnification, high contrast, large text.
* **Colour Blindness** – difficulty distinguishing certain colours (red‑green most common).
* **Cataracts / Glare sensitivity** – need reduced brightness, clean layouts.

quizData.question: A user who can see but needs text to be very large has what type of disability?
quizData.explanation: Low vision refers to partial sight that can't be fully corrected with glasses.

slides.title: Screen Readers: Ears on the Page 🔊
slides.content:
Blind users typically use a **screen reader** that converts the interface into speech or braille.

* It reads text, announces elements ("button", "link"), and navigates by headings, landmarks.
* Users don't use a mouse – they use keyboard shortcuts.
* The **accessibility tree** is what the screen reader 'sees'.

slides.title: How a Screen Reader Sees
slides.content: Example of a button in HTML:

quizData.question: What does a screen reader announce for `<button>Buy now</button>`?
quizData.explanation: Typically: 'Buy now, button' (role announced after the text). Order may vary, but the role is always included.

slides.title: Low Vision & Magnification 🔍
slides.content:
Users with low vision may:

* Use browser zoom (Ctrl + +) up to 400%.
* Use a screen magnifier that enlarges a portion of the screen.
* Need high contrast mode (white on black).
* Rely on strong focus indicators.

**Design must not break at high zoom.** Use relative units, responsive design.

slides.title: Colour Blindness 🎨
slides.content:
About 1 in 12 men have some form of colour blindness.

* **Never use colour alone** to convey information.
* Example error state: red border **and** an icon/text label.
* Ensure sufficient contrast between foreground and background.
* Tools: Coblis (colour blindness simulator), WebAIM contrast checker.

quizData.question: What is wrong with 'Click the green button to continue'?

options.text: It relies solely on colour to convey information

quizData.explanation: A colour‑blind user may not distinguish the green button. Use additional cues like text or icons.
